data.one_liner: Responsive UI scaling from design dimensions and context-free navigation with page transitions.
data.what_it_does: Scales every size written in code using extensions based on a reference design size, handles navigation without requiring a BuildContext, and provides 14 built-in page transitions. It also adapts layouts depending on whether the app runs on a phone, tablet, or desktop.
use_when: You need to implement a design scaled proportionally across different phone and tablet screen sizes.
You require navigation actions to be triggered from anywhere in your codebase without a BuildContext.
You want custom page transitions for Navigator or routers like go_router and auto_route.
avoid_when: You prefer standard Flutter responsive techniques like LayoutBuilder, MediaQuery, or flexible constraints over design-to-screen pixel scaling.
You are already using an alternative responsive scaling framework and want to avoid conflicting scale systems.
strengths: Provides convenient number extensions (.rw, .rh, .rt, .rs) to automatically scale dimensions and fonts.
Includes context-free navigation methods and 14 built-in route animations.
Supports MaterialApp, CupertinoApp, WidgetsApp, and routers like go_router and auto_route.
weaknesses: Forces a strict single design size approach across the app.
Tying UI measurements directly to a fixed design resolution can sometimes cause unexpected layouts on extreme aspect ratios.
data.setup_notes: Wrap your root app widget in Flexify and supply your design width and height.

alternatives.name: responsive_framework
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer scaling and adapting layouts through responsive breakpoints and UI scaling wrappers rather than direct number extensions.

alternatives.name: sizer
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want screen-percentage-based sizing extensions instead of scaling from a fixed design width and height.
